2609.30184.title: ARGUS: Role-Aware Event Knowledge Graphs for U.S. Employment-Discrimination Complaints
2609.30184.paper_summary: U.S. employment-discrimination complaints describe complex event sequences that are not explicitly captured by lexical or embedding-based representations alone. We present ARGUS, a source-grounded pipeline that combines a 5W1H-inspired schema, legal-domain models, and LLM-based structured generation to construct document-level Event Knowledge Graphs (EKGs) from CourtListener complaints. ARGUS extracts fact-bearing statements, builds chunk-level event graphs with participant, temporal, and causal structure, and merges them into document-level representations. We evaluate graph quality through human and multi-model assessment and test downstream utility on claim classification and legal QA. The graph-structured classifier outperforms raw and linearized baselines on the held-out set, and EKG-only retrieval improves document-scoped QA, while open-retrieval gains remain limited by low first-stage candidate recall. These results suggest that EKGs are most useful for organizing and reasoning over evidence once relevant material has been retrieved.
2609.30184.paper_summary_zh: 美國的就業歧視投訴描述了複雜的事件序列，這些序列僅靠詞彙或嵌入基礎的表示無法明確捕捉。我們提出了ARGUS，一個基於來源的流程，結合了5W1H啟發的架構、法律領域模型以及基於LLM的結構化生成，從CourtListener的投訴中構建文檔級事件知識圖（EKGs）。ARGUS提取事實性陳述，構建具有參與者、時間和因果結構的塊級事件圖，並將它們合併為文檔級表示。我們通過人工和多模型評估來評估圖的質量，並在索賠分類和法律問答上測試下游效用。圖結構分類器在保留集上超越了原始和線性基準，而僅使用EKG的檢索改善了文檔範圍的問答，儘管開放檢索的增益仍然受到低第一階段候選回憶的限制。這些結果表明，EKGs在檢索到相關材料後，對於組織和推理證據最為有用。
